exposure: Residency specialty (Internal Medicine, Pediatrics, OB/GYN, General Surgery)
outcome: Personal experiences with pregnancy during training
Perceived support for parental leave coordination
Perceived capability upon return to work
Attitude towards encouraging pregnancy during residency
cohort: The cohort consisted of 278 residents from internal medicine, pediatrics, obstetrics/gynecology, and general surgery programs who had delivered, or whose partner had delivered, during residency.
finding: The study identified differences across specialties in policy and perceptions of pregnancy during training that impact residency quality of life, noting OB/GYN trainees attended fewer prenatal visits while pediatric trainees felt more supported and took longer parental leaves.
